<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="ניסן_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518917921_theRebbe_748" batchId="meluket-_D7_A0_D7_99_D7_A1_D7_9F_meluket__BH_POST_1766518917921_theRebbe_748__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section contains the title and date of the maamar for the last day of Pesach 5714.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">Last day of Pesach 5714*.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the spirit of Hashem and its details of wisdom, understanding, counsel, and might relate to judgment by scent, not only by intellect.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"And the spirit of Hashem shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and fear of Hashem... and he shall judge the poor with righteousness..."¹</t>
    <t s="1">For by means of all these matters resting upon him</t>
    <t s="2">(the spirit of Hashem,</t>
    <t s="3">the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, etc.),</t>
    <t s="4">through this his judgment will be a judgment of righteousness.²</t>
    <t s="5">And it needs to be understood,</t>
    <t s="6">for seemingly,</t>
    <t s="7">the connection of righteous judgment to wisdom and understanding is specifically in judgment according to intellect,</t>
    <t s="8">and since regarding Mashiach it is written³</t>
    <t s="9">"and he shall scent the fear of Hashem," that he smells and judges,</t>
    <t s="10">what relevance does this judgment</t>
    <t s="11">(which is according to scent)</t>
    <t s="12">have to the spirit of wisdom and understanding?</t>
    <t s="13">And the explanation is,</t>
    <t s="14">that "the spirit of Hashem" is a general matter,</t>
    <t s="15">the drawing down of Elokus,</t>
    <t s="16">and "the spirit of wisdom and understanding, etc." are the particulars drawn from the general principle of "the spirit of Hashem."⁴</t>
    <t s="17">And this is the connection of the spirit of wisdom and understanding to "and he shall judge the poor with righteousness, etc.,"</t>
    <t s="18">for wisdom and understanding,</t>
    <t s="19">when they are drawn from the general principle of "the spirit of Hashem,"</t>
    <t s="20">are in a more elevated manner,</t>
    <t s="21">and they are relevant</t>
    <t s="22">(not only to judgment according to intellect, but)</t>
    <t s="23">also to judgment according to scent,</t>
    <t s="24">"he smells and judges."</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the distinction between Atzilus and BiYA as analogous to the body and garments of the soul, clarifying the unique unity of the Sefiros of Atzilus with the Ein Sof.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">2)</t>
    <t s="1">And this will be understood by prefacing what our sages said,⁵</t>
    <t s="2">"The light of Ein Sof is above, above, without end, and below, below, without limit."</t>
    <t s="3">And the precise point in this is known,⁶</t>
    <t s="4">for the matter of "above" and "below"</t>
    <t s="5">(even "above" and "below" in spirituality⁷)</t>
    <t s="6">is a limitation,</t>
    <t s="7">and how can it be said regarding Ein Sof</t>
    <t s="8">(may He be blessed)</t>
    <t s="9">that He is "above, etc." and "below, etc."?</t>
    <t s="10">And seemingly it could be said that the matter of "above" and "below" is in the worlds</t>
    <t s="11">(and not in Ein Sof),</t>
    <t s="12">and the explanation of "the light of Ein Sof is above, etc. and below, etc." is that He exists</t>
    <t s="13">(and spreads)</t>
    <t s="14">in all the levels of all the worlds,</t>
    <t s="15">"above, above, without end, and below, below, without limit."</t>
    <t s="16">But according to this, it should have said "there is no place empty of Him"⁸</t>
    <t s="17">(and the like),</t>
    <t s="18">and not "above, etc." and "below, etc.,"⁹</t>
    <t s="19">which divides into two matters, etc.</t>
    <t s="20">And behold, the Admo"r Mahara"sh explains,¹⁰</t>
    <t s="21">that in order to understand this matter</t>
    <t s="22">(that "the light of Ein Sof is above without end and below without limit")</t>
    <t s="23">one must first preface the matter of Atzilus and BiYA.¹¹</t>
    <t s="24">For the distinction between Atzilus and BiYA is as stated in the Tikkunim in the discourse of "Patah Eliyahu,"¹²</t>
    <t s="25">"You have fashioned several bodies which are called bodies in relation to the garments that cover them,"</t>
    <t s="26">that the Sefiros of Atzilus are "bodies,"</t>
    <t s="27">and BiYA</t>
    <t s="28">(even the Sefiros of BiYA¹³)</t>
    <t s="29">are garments for the Sefiros of Atzilus, which are clothed and covered within them.</t>
    <t s="30">And the Alter Rebbe explains in the discourse "Patah Eliyahu,"¹⁴</t>
    <t s="31">that the distinction between "bodies" and "garments"</t>
    <t s="32">(Atzilus and BiYA)</t>
    <t s="33">will be understood from the distinction between a body and a garment as it is in a human,</t>
    <t s="34">"From my flesh I shall perceive G-d."¹⁵</t>
    <t s="35">For the human body,</t>
    <t s="36">even though it is only a garment for the soul</t>
    <t s="37">(as it is written,¹⁶</t>
    <t s="38">"You have clothed me with skin and flesh"),</t>
    <t s="39">is unified with the soul,</t>
    <t s="40">unlike garments which are separate from the person</t>
    <t s="41">(even from the person's body).</t>
    <t s="42">And behold, the matter of body and garments also exists in the spiritual powers drawn from the soul.</t>
    <t s="43">For intellect and emotions are the "body" of the human soul,</t>
    <t s="44">and thought, speech, and action are the garments of the soul.</t>
    <t s="45">That is,</t>
    <t s="46">the soul itself is above even intellect and emotions,</t>
    <t s="47">and intellect and emotions are only garments for the soul,</t>
    <t s="48">for through its clothing in them, it performs specific actions</t>
    <t s="49">(to think,</t>
    <t s="50">to love, etc.),</t>
    <t s="51">except that intellect and emotions are unified with the soul,</t>
    <t s="52">unlike thought, speech, and action, which are separate garments.</t>
    <t s="53">And the explanation of this</t>
    <t s="54">(that intellect and emotions are unified with the soul,</t>
    <t s="55">and thought, speech, and action are separate),</t>
    <t s="56">is that the distinction between a unified garment and a separate garment is,</t>
    <t s="57">that a separate garment can be removed,</t>
    <t s="58">unlike a unified garment</t>
    <t s="59">(like the body)</t>
    <t s="60">which cannot be removed.</t>
    <t s="61">And this is that thought, speech, and action are separate garments, and intellect and emotions are unified garments,</t>
    <t s="62">for speech and action can be removed,</t>
    <t s="63">"a time to speak and a time to be silent from speaking,"¹⁷</t>
    <t s="64">and also thought, which is constant,</t>
    <t s="65">behold, one can exchange one thought for another without any effort.</t>
    <t s="66">Unlike intellect and emotions,</t>
    <t s="67">since they are unified with the soul,</t>
    <t s="68">in order to change them,</t>
    <t s="69">effort is required.¹⁸</t>
    <t s="70">And furthermore,</t>
    <t s="71">there are matters in intellect and emotions that cannot be changed</t>
    <t s="72">(even through effort),</t>
    <t s="73">for they are according to the nature of his soul.¹⁹</t>
    <t s="74">And this is why the Sefiros of Atzilus are called "bodies" and BiYA "garments,"</t>
    <t s="75">for the three worlds of BiYA are analogous to thought, speech, and action</t>
    <t s="76">[Beriah is thought,</t>
    <t s="77">Yetzirah is speech,</t>
    <t s="78">and Asiyah is action]</t>
    <t s="79">which are separate garments,</t>
    <t s="80">unlike the Sefiros of Atzilus,</t>
    <t s="81">even though they are incomparable to the light of Ein Sof, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="82">they are unified with the light of Ein Sof that is clothed within them,</t>
    <t s="83">"He and His organs are one,"²⁰</t>
    <t s="84">and therefore they are called "bodies,"</t>
    <t s="85">for they are like the body which, even though it is incomparable to the soul, is nevertheless unified with the soul.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
